Convergent Synthesis of Tetrasaccharide Fragment of Cervimycin K
Jihun Kang and Young Ho Rhee *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 4468 −4472 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: A new synthetic approach toward oligosaccharides consisting only of 2,3,6-trideoxypyranoglycosides is reported. The
key feature is highlighted by the convergent approach that allows the introduction of the aglycon moiety in the late stage of the
synthesis. As an illustrative example, the tetrasaccharide portion of cervimycin K was prepared as cyclohexyl glycoside.
2-Deoxyoligosaccharides are present in numerous bioactive
natural products as a conjugate form to complex aglycon
moieties. The length and structure of these oligosaccharides
are reported to have a signi ﬁcant e ﬀect on the bioactivities of
the natural products.
1 Thus, the stereocontrolled synthesis of
2-deoxyoligosaccharides represents one of the most funda-
mental topics in glycochemistry.
2,3 This topic has been
considered very challenging because of the lack of stereo-
directing appendages at the 2 position. This problem is
particularly well-addressed by oligosaccharides consisting only
of 2,3,6-trideoxypyranoglycosides (such as amicetose or
rhodinose) linked by both α-o r β- anomeric con ﬁgurations.
They constitute the glycosidic part of several natural products
such as lycoperdinoside B,
4 amicenomycin A,5 and cervimycin
K6 (Scheme 1 ). Despite the relatively short length and simple
structure of these oligosaccharides, their stereocontrolled
syntheses have been very limited in conventional glycochem-
istry, because of the poor stability of the anomeric
conﬁguration.
7
Recently, O ’Doherty reported a potential solution to this
problem based upon the iterative use of the Pd-catalyzed
reaction of a pyranose unit (A in Scheme 1 ).
8−11 Later, Tang
further elaborated on the stereodivergent coupling by
introducing related catalytic asymmetric transformations.
9
This de novo approach represents a signi ﬁcant advance in the
synthesis of 2,3,6-trideoxyoligosaccharides. However, incorpo-
ration of the method into the total synthesis needs to
overcome another hurdle in that structurally complex aglycons
should be introduced in an early stage and carried through the
subsequent stepwise oligosaccharide synthesis. In this regard, a
convergent method that couples the aglycon and glycon
portions in a late stage would be highly advantageous.
Recently, we reported Pd-catalyzed asymmetric hydroalkox-

ylation of ene-alkoxyallenes possessing glycosidic portion (B in
Scheme 1).12,13 This method was successfully evolved into the
convergent total synthesis of 11-deoxylandomycin natural
products, upon combination with sequential catalysis com-
posed of ring-closing-metathesis (RCM) and Pd-catalyzed
hydrogenation. Upon the basis of these precedents, we
envisioned that an analogous approach can successfully ful ﬁll
the above-mentioned goal in the synthesis of 2,3,6-trideox-
yoligosaccharides. As a proof-of-concept example, we report
here a convergent synthesis of the tetrasaccharide moiety of
antibacterial cervimycin K as a cyclohexyl glycoside.
14,15
From a retrosynthetic viewpoint, the synthesis of target 1
necessitates preparation of ene-alkoxyallene 2 (Scheme 2). We
reasoned that this intermediate can be readily prepared by
convergent coupling of 3 with alcohol 4. Both of these
compounds would be then derived from commercially
available diacetyl-6-deoxy-( L)-glucal 5.
The synthesis commenced with the preparation of allene 3
(Scheme 3 ). Reaction of 5 and alcohol 6 in the presence of
stoichiometric BF
3·OEt2 followed by the deacetylation
generated allylic alcohol 7 in 49% yield (over two steps) as a
single diastereomer. Inversion of this alcohol under Mitsunobu
conditions provided 8 in 76% yield. From this compound,
allene 3 was prepared in 62% yield via a four-step event
combining (i) benzylation of the alcohol, (ii) chemoselective
removal of the PMB group,
16 (iii) propargylation of the
resulting alcohol, and (iv) ba se-catalyzed isomerization.
Alcohol 4 was uneventfully prepared from 9 in 42% overall
yield using an analogous procedure to that for 8 (for the
detailed information, see the SI).
Having prepared 3 and 4, we then examined the Pd-
catalyzed coupling reaction. As depicted in Scheme 4, an initial
reaction in the presence of Pd 2(dba)3 (2.5 mol %), standard
(S,S)-Trost ligand L (5 mol %), and triethylamine (0.1 equiv)
in toluene at 40 °C for 2 h generated the acyclic acetal 10 in
94% yield. Even though the diastereoselectivity of this reaction
could not be veri ﬁed at this stage, we decided to see if the
RCM reaction of this compound would deliver the desired
trisaccharide 11 (path A, Scheme 4 ). A preliminary reaction
using a ﬁrst generation Grubbs catalyst was very slow.
Switching to a second generation catalyst (10 mol %)
signiﬁcantly improved the conversion (>90%). However, the
target compound 11 was obtained in only 20% yield.
Interestingly, two additional compounds 12 and 13 containing
a dihydrofuran skeleton were also obtained in signi ﬁcant 76%
combined yield. Apparently, these compounds are formed by
the ring-rearrangement metathesis (RRM) of 10 (path B,
Scheme 4 ).
17 Subjection of 11 to similar conditions again
produced 12 and 13 as the major products. This result strongly
suggests that the products are formed in a reversible manner.
To assess the diastereoselectivity of the Pd-catalyzed reaction,
we attempted the synthesis of 14 (diastereomeric to 10) using
an enantiomeric ( R,R)-ligand. As depicted in Scheme 4 , this
reaction turned out to be signi ﬁcantly slower. Complete
assumption of the starting materials required the use of 10 mol
%P d
2(dba)3 precatalyst. In this case, 14 was obtained in 86%
yield. Because the 1H NMR spectrum of this compound was
indistinguishable from 10, we performed the RCM reaction of
14. Again, this reaction produced a mixture of desired 15 and
dihydrofuran derivatives analogous to 12 and 13. Even though

chromatographic separation of 15 was troublesome, it could be
puriﬁed by recrystallization from the crude mixture. The 1H
NMR spectra of 11 and 15 with respect to the newly generated
stereocenter were clearly distinguishable, thus con ﬁrming the
excellent ligand-driven stereoselectivity in the Pd-catalyzed
reactions (for the detailed analysis, see the Supporting
Information).
Because the synthesis of trisaccharide moiety 11 by way of
RCM reaction was unsuccessful, we decided to carry the
acyclic acetal 10 forward without RCM reaction. For this
purpose, compound 10 was ﬁrst converted into allene 16 using
the procedure optimized in Scheme 3 (for detailed
information, see the Supporting Information ). Then, we
examined the sequential Pd −Ru catalysis of this compound
using primary alcohol 17 or secondary alcohol 18 as the
coupling partner. A preliminary reaction of 16 with 17 in the
presence of an ( R,R)-ligand under optimized conditions
smoothly proceeded to produce the adduct in 93% yield
with 21:1 ratio. The subsequent RCM reaction was sluggish.
Complete conversion required the use of 30 mol % of a second
generation Grubbs catalyst. Nevertheless, the desired tetra-
saccharide 19a was obtained in 92% yield apparently with no
competition from the RRM reaction ( Table 1 ).
18 Using an
enantiomeric ( S,S)-ligand reversed the s tereoselectivity,
generating 19b possessing all the stereochemical features of
the glycosidic part in cervimycin K in 81% yield with high 17:1
selectivity over two steps. In the case of secondary alcohol 18,
the Pd-catalyzed coupling reaction turned out to be slower,
presumably due to the increased steric congestion of the
substrate. Using a higher loading of Pd
2(dba)3 (10 mol %) was
necessary to obtain the acyclic adduct in high 90% yield. The
subsequent RCM reaction smoothly proceeded to give 20a in
86% yield. Finally, diastereomeric 20b, a key intermediate in
our synthesis, was produced in 54% yield (over two steps) with
13:1 selectivity again with the use of an enantiomeric ( S,S)-
ligand.
Our ﬁnal task was to synthesize the target cyclohexyl
glycoside 1 from 20b, which required the execution of two
events: (i) hydrogenation of the ole ﬁn and (ii) removal of the
benzyl group. Initial e ﬀorts toward one-pot operation using
various Pd catalysts were unsuccessful, because of the extensive
decomposition of 20b possessing labile anomeric centers.
Thus, the ole ﬁnw a s ﬁrst hydrogenated using o-nitro-
benzenesulfonyl-hydrazide (NBSH). As depicted in Scheme
5, this method a ﬀorded 21 in 91% yield.
19 Removal of the
benzyl group proceeded smoothly by using a Pd/C catalyst
under a hydrogen atmosphere , which delivered target
compound 1 in 98% yield. The structure of 1 depicted in
Scheme 5 was rigorously veri ﬁed by various two-dimensional
NMR spectroscopic techniques. (for detailed information, see
the Supporting Information ). Overall, tetrasaccharide 1 was
assembled by the asymmetric sequential metal catalysis (Pd −
Ru−Pd) from commercially available starting material 5.O n
the basis of a ligand-driven stereodivergent process, various
stereoisomers of 1 can also be accessed with comparable
eﬃciency to that for the naturally occurring structure.
In summary, we developed a new synthetic strategy toward
2,3,6-trideoxyoligosaccharid e. Remarkably, the convergent
nature makes the method particularly amenable to the total
synthesis of the related natural products. As an illustrative
example, the ﬁrst synthesis of tetrasaccharide moiety in
cervimycin K has been achieved. Currently, we are working
on expanding of the scope of our de novo strategy to other
oligosaccharides as well as on the total synthesis of related
natural products. The results of this study will be reported in
due course.
